sources.citation: Pelkey, Jamin. 2011. A Phula Comparative Lexicon: Phola, Phuza, Muji, Phowa, Azha. SIL Language and Culture Documentation and Description 18. Dallas: SIL International. 144 pp.
sources.note: §3.3 'Southern Muji phonology in brief' (pp. 8-9): 'Regarding suprasegmental phonology, Southern Muji features five pitch contrasts.. /55/, /33/, /13/, /21/ and /52/'; sandhi and tense-voice phonation described. MLT Muzi (Gejiu, Laochang, Malutang) is listed only as an external datapoint in the abbreviations and footnotes. a full-text search for stress/accent/prominence: no hits in 536 kB of text.

sources.note: Intelligibility/RTT rationale only (Muzi speakers scored.50 on the Southern Muji recorded text test); cites Pelkey forthcoming 2008 La Trobe dissertation as the sole published source. Nothing on phonology.

sources.citation: Pelkey, Jamin R. 2007. Muji's mirrored merger: correlative redistribution of checked tone classes in a newly defined Burmic cluster. Mon-Khmer Studies 37: 179-195.
sources.note: Sec. 2 'Sample phonology sketch' (pp. 181-183) sketches Southern Muji PJZ (syllable C(V)VT, 34 initials, 5 tones 55/33/13/21/52, tone sandhi, non-contrastive phonation); Muzi enters only as tone-data points MLT (Malutang, Gejiu) and SZT (Shizitou, Jinping). No mention of stress, accent or prominence anywhere in the 17 pages.
